account:
Today has been oddly thin on actual town business despite my appointments. I attended the mill for the ten o'clock grain inspection, but no miller or responsible manager appeared. I saw 68 hay bales for sale at two emeralds each; that establishes stock, not grain quality or satisfactory accounts. The inspection remains incomplete. The secretary has been unable to identify the manager. At the council-letters appointment, neither of us had any council correspondence, and the secretary says none has reached them.

The unusual matter is the repeated talk of a bridge or port change at the bakery. Townsfolk 21 reported versions naming the baker, innkeeper, builder, freight and neighbour as having been there. Several other townsfolk repeated the general rumour. Those are reports, not conversations I witnessed, and I do not yet know whether they describe one meeting or several, or even an agreed proposal. I tried to ask the baker directly, but did not obtain an answer. I suspect people may be discussing a transport or trade project without bringing it to my office, but I have no evidence of its purpose, terms, or any deliberate effort to exclude me.

The secretary says they will seek a mill contact and invite the actual bridge or port proposers to explain matters tomorrow morning. My subsequent dictation of a mill letter was not heard, so I cannot assume it will be drafted. My next appointment is tea with the neighbour at the east-bank cottage at 15:00; the neighbour may have firsthand information, given the reports, but that remains to be established. Later I have office time at 16:30 and the builder's great-hall lighting inspection at 18:00. The builder has reportedly said the hall lanterns are in good order; I have no basis to connect that inspection with the bakery discussions.
